# <span id="aanchor498"></span> Live Oil Info

This feature requires the **Liquids System** module and **Live Oil Management** add-on. The **Live Oil Service (FlowCal.LiveOil.Service.exe)** must be installed as well.

Live Oil Management allows users to set up meters to hold low vapor pressure (“dead”) oil quantities and associated flash gas volumes. These holding meters receive periodic flow data calculated by applying user-provided shrink and flash gas factors to the production volume of a related high vapor pressure (“live”) oil meter. The holding meters are otherwise independent and operate like typical meters: They can have analyses applied for component calculations, they can be included in balances, they can be closed and receive PPAs, and they have their own validations.

In practice, a crude oil liquid meter is designated as a live oil meter, and child meters for dead oil and flash gas are created directly from this meter (Meter Editor \> Tools \> Live Oil Info).

Dead oil and flash gas meters receive data from the parent live oil meter:

Dead oil NSV = live oil theoretical production \* units correction

Flash gas volume = live oil theoretical production \* flash gas factor \* units correction \* pb correction

Data is transferred from live oil to dead oil and flash gas meters using the installed Live Oil service (FlowCal.LiveOil.Service.exe). This service is available on the [Service Queues](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Queues.md) and [Service Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Configuration.md) forms. (See: [Live Oil Service](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Live%20Oil%20Service.md))

Shrink factor, flash gas factor, and stock tank density are fully implemented and can be imported into sources and applied to meters or imported into liquid meters directly.

Default validations are available for flash gas and shrink factors. Shrink factors, if provided, must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 1. Flash gas factors, if provided, must be greater than or equal to 0. In addition, if Live Oil Management is authorized, then exceptions will be generated if either the shrink factor or flash gas factor is missing.

A theoretical production calculation method is also available to allow users to choose between the standard API 20.1 application of shrink factor and the direct application of the shrink factor to NSV.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Live Oil Management form:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**.
2.  Click the **Tools** menu option.
3.  Select any liquid meter or a flash gas meter.
4.  Select **Live Oil Management**.

The **Liquid System** module and **Live Oil Management** add-on must be authorized to enable the Live Oil Management form. The Live Oil Management form is not available when the Meter Editor is in New or Edit mode.

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

- **Live Oil** - When the checkbox is selected, the liquid meter is designated as a live oil parent meter. This option must be selected for all other options on this tab to be enabled.
- **Stabilized Oil** – If this checkbox is not selected, the shrink factor and flash gas factor must be assigned a value for the calculation of dead oil and flash gas meter volumes.
- **Live Oil (Parent)** – This group box contains the meter number, meter name, and system for any meter that is designated as a live oil meter. These fields will be read-only and will be auto-populated with the live oil meter information.
- **Dead Oil (Child)** – Use this group box to create a dead oil meter and link it to a parent live oil meter.
  <div class="procedure">

  To create a dead oil meter:

  1.  Click the **Edit** button at the bottom of the Live Oil Management screen.
  2.  Enter a system, meter number, and meter name for the dead oil meter.
  3.  If the dead oil and live oil meter relationship is active, select the "Active" checkbox. This checkbox selection is not datetime effective.

  A dead oil meter can only be assigned to one live oil meter.

  </div>
- **Flash Gas (Child)** – Use this group box to create a flash gas meter and link it to a parent live oil meter.
  <div class="procedure">

  To create a Flash Gas meter:

  1.  Click the **Edit** button at the bottom of the Live Oil Management screen.
  2.  Enter a system, meter number, and meter name for the flash gas meter.
  3.  If the flash gas and live oil meter relationship is active, select the "Active" checkbox. This checkbox selection is not datetime effective.

  The **Gas System** module must be authorized to create flash gas meters. A flash gas meter can only be assigned to one live oil meter.

  </div>
